title: Start of Drug Coverage under a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
Drug coverage on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan comes into force on the date the plan's effective date rule produces from the day the plan received the completed election form. CMS has returned an accepting transaction reply code for that drug plan enrollment, and that code is recorded on the enrollment record, before coverage is brought into force; the reply code on the record is the authority for it.

Under the rule that an election takes effect on the first of the month following receipt, an election received in any month takes effect on the first day of the next month. An election made in the annual election period takes effect on 1 January of the following contract year.

Effectuation opens the member's payment stage: at the deductible stage where the plan carries a deductible, and directly at initial coverage where it does not.

Retroactive effectuation happens only where CMS directs it, and only as far back as the months of retroactive coverage the plan elected allows. A member who paid cash at the pharmacy during a retroactive period is reimbursed on a direct member reimbursement claim rather than by repricing the pharmacy's own claim.

## Worked dates, on hypothetical receipts

- A completed election form received on 12 March, outside the annual election period, takes effect on 1 April.
- A completed election form received on the last day of a month, again outside the annual election period, takes effect on the first day of the month that follows it.
- A completed election form received on 3 November, inside the annual election period, takes effect on 1 January of the following contract year.

In each case the date runs from the day the plan received the completed form, and in each case coverage is brought into force only once the accepting CMS reply code stands on the enrollment record.
